audit.why: Lane difficulty framing (poke-heavy early, Vlad scales) matches kits and 59.39% WR at 884 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart marks Levels 4-5 as Azir and Level 6/items as Skill while content win[] and the packet chart both say Vladimir from row 3 on.
audit.why: Q heal outpaces soldier chip by 4-5 and Vlad's 59% WR supports the flip; the two layers must agree.
audit.corrected: phases[3..6].side -> Vladimir, matching win[3..6] which already read Vladimir.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns has no numbers; Emperor's Divide wall-cuts-retreat interaction absent; two Do's/Don'ts bodies are pasted tradeGood/tradeBad.
audit.why: Azir E is 22s at rank 1 (16 max), Vlad W 28s early, Vlad R 120s — real numbers make the advice concrete; Vlad has no dash so the R wall is a genuine kill tool against him.

audit.whatIsWrong: suspectNames flags 'His Emperor's Divide' but Emperor's Divide IS Azir's real R name — false positive.
audit.why: Kit file confirms R = Emperor's Divide.
audit.corrected: No name change needed; spikes[1].text rewritten anyway to add the wall-cuts-retreat interaction.

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. It governs your forward steps. - W Sanguine Pool spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Azir Shifting Sands: 22s cooldown at rank 1, 16 at max — once the shield-dash is burnt you own his longest window; step forward then. - Sanguine Pool is 28s early: spent on poke, the real engage lands unanswered. - The 120s R closes arguments, not opens them.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, E-charge as he steps to answer, release and walk — the trade costs him HP and pays yours.
edits.after: Hold Sanguine Pool for his Shifting Sands engage or a dive — its 28-second early cooldown means you get one 'no' per fight.

edits.before: Pooling his poke and then eating the real engage at half HP with nothing — the pool is a combo-breaker, not a flinch reflex.
edits.after: Tides of Blood spends your own health — charging it low inside soldier range hands Azir exactly the kill window his poke was building toward.

edits.before: Azir wins by landing Shifting Sands, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Azir wins by chipping you with soldier pokes you can't answer pre-4, then walling off your dashless retreat with Emperor's Divide in ganks.

edits.before: His Emperor's Divide is a game-ender in skirmishes but does little to a fed Vladimir 1v1; your Hemoplague amp beats his ult in raw lane trades.
edits.after: His Emperor's Divide can wall off your retreat — you have no dash, so save Flash or pool for the knockback; your Hemoplague amp still wins the raw 1v1.
